latest_release.name: CodeAssist 3.46.0
latest_release.body:
# 🚀 CodeAssist 3.46.0

**MODERN JAVA IN THE RUN CONSOLE**
- **Java 17 to 21 programs run** on your phone: records, sealed types, pattern `switch` (type patterns, `case null`, guards, enums) and the newer library methods such as `List.of`, `getFirst()`, `stream.toList()`, `String.formatted` and `Math.clamp`, even on an Android version that does not have them
- **Virtual threads, `ScopedValue` and `StructuredTaskScope`** compile and run (emulated on real threads, up to 2,000 at once), in both their Java 21 and Java 25 shapes
- Records work as map keys and in sets, and print `boolean` and `char` components correctly
- Console programs run **two to three times faster**
- Arrays handed to library code (`list.add`, `ByteBuffer.wrap`, `Arrays.asList`) are now shared with it instead of copied
- Fixed: `0.0 == -0.0`, array `instanceof` and casts, `ArrayStoreException`, catching a stack overflow or a negative array size, and string constant identity
- Fixed: `compareBy({ it.a }, { it.b })` ended a run with "Array has incompatible type"

**RELEASE BUILDS (R8)**
- A release build with **shrinking on no longer fails on Android 12 and older** (`NoSuchMethodError: readAllBytes`, and two more of the same kind)
- A release build **survives R8 running out of memory**: it shrinks your own code and packages the libraries unshrunk, instead of failing with no APK. The console says when this happened
- Raising the R8 heap makes the next build try the full shrink again
- **Library keep rules** shipped inside an AAR now reach R8, so a minified app no longer loses what a library reaches by reflection
- The out-of-memory error names the heap R8 really had and whether the setting can go higher on your device

**EDITOR**
- **Import static**: an unresolved `assertEquals(...)` in Java now offers `Import static org.junit.Assert.assertEquals`, from library classes and from your own project's Java classes
- The Kotlin **Import** fix offers a Java class's static method too
- A Java **text block** (`"""`) is highlighted as one string across its lines
- The **rename** prompt has Rename and Cancel buttons, the on-screen keyboard's action key confirms rename and go-to-line, and Back closes them
- Fixed: `use { }` on a class declared `: AutoCloseable` was an unresolved reference, and so was `import kotlin.use`
- Fixed: a function ending in `mutex.withLock { return x }` was reported as missing a return, and code after a `return@run` was marked unreachable
- Fixed: accepting an override from the completion list left the dot that opened it
- Go to declaration and the color swatch of a **library resource** open the right file

**LANGUAGES**
- **Choose the interface language** in Settings > Appearance, without changing the phone's language
- **Every screen is translated** in Arabic, Spanish, Indonesian, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian and Chinese, including the layout designer and the Git panel
- Under a right-to-left language, a view dragged in the layout designer follows your finger

**AI ASSISTANT**
- A custom gateway can **fetch its model list**: pick a model instead of typing its name
- **Enter breaks the line** in the chat field on an on-screen keyboard; it sends only with a physical keyboard
- Fixed: every request failing with "The compiled grammar is too large" once the tool set grew
- Fixed: with the **MCP server** turned on, the app failed to start below Android 14, and a connecting client closed it

**RUN AND BUILD**
- Fixed: Run failing with **"Too many active sessions"** after several install prompts were dismissed
- The build log says **how long each slow task took**, and the build time no longer includes waiting on the install screen
- A unit test can read files in `src/test/resources`

**FIXES**
- Fixed a freeze on first launch on devices with slow storage
- Fixed a crash in the Projects Store feed when two sections shared an id
- A project whose source folder is the project folder itself (no `src`) no longer indexes, searches or compiles its own build outp

detail.readme:
# CodeAssist [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/tyron12233/CodeAssist/ci.yml?branch=main&label=CI)](https://github.com/tyron12233/CodeAssist/actions) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/tyron12233/CodeAssist?display_name=tag&sort=semver)](https://github.com/tyron12233/CodeAssist/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/tyron12233/CodeAssist)](LICENSE) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/chat-Discord-5865F2)](https://discord.gg/y2gycT6pDW) CodeAssist is an IDE for Android that runs on Android. You can write Kotlin and Java, preview Compose and XML layouts, and build, sign and install APKs on the phone itself, without a computer or a remote build server. A desktop version for Windows and Linux is built from the same code.

## Features - Kotlin and Java editing: completion, auto-import, errors as you type with quick fixes, go to definition/implementation, reformat and optimize imports. - Android XML completion and validation for layouts, manifests and resource files. - Compose `@Preview` functions render next to the code and update as you edit. XML layouts preview too, including your own custom views. - Builds run on the device: aapt2, kotlinc, ecj, D8/R8 and apksigner. Builds are incremental. Output can be a debug APK, or a release APK or App Bundle signed with your own key. - Multi-module projects, build variants, ViewBinding, AIDL, KSP (Room, Hilt) and Firebase's `google-services.json`. - Dependencies from Maven Central, Google's Maven repository, and local JAR and AAR files. - Import an existing Gradle project, or export a project as a Gradle project to open in Android Studio. - Git: clone, commit, branch, merge, stash and push. With a GitHub sign-in you can clone private repositories and open pull requests. - An optional AI coding agent that uses your own API key (Anthropic, Gemini, OpenAI or OpenRouter). - Plugins can add languages, build steps, tool windows and project templates. C/C++ (NDK) support is a separate plugin. ## Limitations - CodeAssist does not run Gradle. Build scripts are read when a project is imported (dependencies, version catalogs, the common `android {}` options), but Gradle plugins and custom build logic are not executed. - Only the bundled Kotlin compiler plugins are available: Compose, kotlinx.serialization and Parcelize. - Kotlin support is newer than Java support and has more rough edges. - Large projects are slow to index and build on phones with little RAM. If something you need is missing, open an issue. It helps to know what people are trying to build. ## Download - [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/tyron12233/CodeAssist/releases): the Android APK, and the desktop builds for Windows and Linux. - [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.tyron.code) The Play build and the GitHub APK are signed with different keys, so one can't be installed over the other. ## How it works Gradle is too heavy to run on a phone, so CodeAssist keeps its own project model. Each module's build is a graph of tasks with up-to-date checks, much like Gradle's, and the tasks call the Android tools directly instead of going through the Android Gradle Plugin. Changing one file only re-runs the tasks that depend on it. Java analysis uses Eclipse JDT. Kotlin uses the Kotlin compiler's parser with CodeAssist's own analysis on top, so completion doesn't have to start a full compiler session on every keystroke. Symbol indexes for libraries and the Android SDK are stored on disk and read in place, which keeps memory use flat as projects grow. Compose previews don't install anything. The project's compiled code runs in a bytecode interpreter inside the IDE, against the real Compose runtime. More detail is in [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md), and the full list of documents is in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md). ## Building from source You need JDK 17 or newer (CI uses JDK 25). The Android SDK is only needed for the full build. ```sh # Core modules only: plain JVM, no Android SDK needed CI_CORE_ONLY=true ./gradlew check # Everything, including the Compose UI and the Android app ./gradlew build # Run the desktop IDE ./gradlew :ide-desktop:run # Build the Android app ./gradlew :ide-android:assembleDebug ``` ## Project layout ``` platform/ core services with no IDE-specific knowledge; everything depends on it lang/ the language SPI, indexes, analysis, and the Java/Kotlin/XML backends build-system/ the incremental task engine and the JVM build pipelines run/ running project code on device: interpreter, bytecode VM, AWT/Swing android/ Android support: facets, variants, SDK data, layout preview services/ dependencies, version control, the project store, analytics, the AI agent plugins/ the plugin SPI and the host that loads plugins app/ the Compose UI and the Android, desktop and command-line launchers tools/ test harnesses ``` Gradle project paths are flat (`:lang-kotlin` lives in `lang/lang-kotlin`); `settings.gradle.kts` maps them. [docs/modules.md](docs/modules.md) describes each module. ## Tests and benchmarks Completion quality, editor latency, indexing and build performance are checked against committed baselines by the `regressionTest` tasks. The numbers below are regenerated on each release. | Area | Metric | Result | |---|---|---| | Java completion **quality** | recall / top-1 / MRR | **100%** / 75% / 0.88 | | Java completion **latency** (per keystroke) | member access / type ref | **4.3 ms** / 2.8 ms | | Symbol **index** quality | recall / top-1 / MRR | **100%** / 90% / 0.95 | | Symbol **index** query | prefix / fuzzy | ~4.4 µs / ~56 ns | Recall is how often the expected item appears in the completion list at all, top-1 how often it is first, and MRR the average of 1/rank. Latency is measured on the maintainer's machine, so treat it as a rough figure. **2595** tests passing across **442** suites · 0 failing · 4 skipped (framework / `CI_CORE_ONLY`). ## Contributing Bug reports and pull requests are welcome. For anything larger than a small fix, open an issue first so we can agree on the approach. Before sending a pull request, run `CI_CORE_ONLY=true ./gradlew check`; it is what CI runs. Plugin authors should start with [docs/writing-plugins.md](docs/writing-plugins.md). For questions and discussion, join the [Discord server](https://discord.gg/y2gycT6pDW). ## License CodeAssist is licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0 or later. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). The plugin SPI modules (`plugin-api`, `plugin-ui-api`, `platform-core`, `vfs-api`, `project-model-api`, `language-api`, `index-api`, `analysis-api` and `build-api`, published under `io.github.tyron12233`) also carry the Classpath exception (see [LICENSE-EXCEPTION](LICENSE-EXCEPTION)), so a plugin compiled against them can use any license.
